rules.topic: Tinkers' fluid unit system in mB: 1 metal ingot = 90, 1 nugget = 10, 1 metal block = 810, 1 gem = 100, 1 gem shard = 25, 1 brick = 250, 1 glass block (or obsidian) = 1000; these differ from the 100/1000 mB conventions of most other mods, so cross-mod fluid math must convert

rules.quote: private static final int CAPACITY_PER_BLOCK = FluidValues.INGOT * 12;
rules.topic: Smeltery tank capacity: 1080 mB per internal (interior) block of the structure, i.e. 12 ingots per interior block; capacity grows with the interior volume, not with wall count
Smeltery fuel consumption scales with structure size: every 15 wall blocks add 1 to the fuel rate multiplier, so oversized shells burn fuel faster for the same interior volume

Smeltery fuel data (jar defaults, datapack-overridable): lava burns at temperature 1000, one burn cycle consumes 50 mB over a duration of 100 ticks at rate 10; a fuel's temperature caps which materials can melt (melting temperature must be below fuel temperature)

rules.quote: private static final int TANK_CAPACITY = FluidValues.INGOT * 24;
rules.topic: Single-block melter tank capacity: 2160 mB (24 ingots); the melter processes one item at a time and is the early-game alternative to the smeltery

Melting is recipe data: each entry states input, fluid result amount, required temperature and time in ticks; example default: an iron ingot melts to 90 mB molten iron at 800 degrees in 60 ticks; lava (1000 degrees) can melt iron but not materials whose temperature exceeds 1000

Alloys are defined as data recipes under data/tconstruct/recipes/smeltery/alloys/ (bronze, brass, constantan, amethyst bronze, bendalloy, cinderslime and more): an alloy forms automatically in the tank when its component fluids are present in the stated ratio and total; exact ratios live in those JSON files (layer 1 data), not in code constants

rules.quote: protected static final LoadableField<Integer,ItemCastingRecipe> COOLING_TIME_FIELD = IntLoadable.FROM_ONE.requiredField("cooling_time", ItemCastingRecipe::getCoolingTime);
rules.topic: Casting recipes state their fluid amount and cooling_time in data; there is no global cooling formula, so per-cast wait times must be read from the recipe (layer 1) — a cast that looks stuck is usually still inside its cooling_time

Tool material definitions, stats (durability, mining speed, attack, traits) and material recipes are datapack data under data/tconstruct/tinkering/materials/, not code; answer material questions from the live-extracted data (layer 2) of the actual pack, since packs and addons override them

rules.quote: // if we have an ore rate, apply it to the output for the foundry
rules.topic: Melting recipes may carry an ore rate and byproducts that apply in the foundry (the ore-processing variant of the smeltery): the same input yields more primary fluid plus byproduct fluids in a foundry than in a smeltery; the rates are per-recipe data
